name: Babylon, the lady of kingdoms
charge: Showing no mercy to the captives; saying, I am, and none else beside me; trusting in her sorceries
summary: Babylon was the Lord's hammer against Judah, and was judged for how she swung it: without mercy, laying a heavy yoke on the ancient, and saying in her heart, I shall be a lady for ever. Isaiah and Jeremiah both name the end before the beginning: the Medes, the sudden fall, the perpetual desolation.
offense: I was wroth with my people, I have polluted mine inheritance, and given them into thine hand: thou didst shew them no mercy; upon the ancient hast thou very heavily laid thy yoke. And thou saidst, I shall be a lady for ever. Thou hast trusted in thy wickedness: thou hast said, None seeth me. Thy wisdom and thy knowledge, it hath perverted thee; and thou hast said in thine heart, I am, and none else beside me. Jeremiah adds the account: they have devoured Israel; the violence done to me and to my flesh be upon Babylon, shall the inhabitant of Zion say.
judgment: The Lord commanded her to sit in the dust and announced the loss of her former honor. Widowhood and loss of children would come suddenly despite her enchantments. An evil she could not ward off would expose the weakness of the wisdom in which she trusted. The astrologers would be as stubble before fire, unable to deliver even themselves. Those with whom she had labored would wander away, leaving none to save her. The oracle reverses Babylon's confidence at every point: power, learning, commerce, and sorcery could not exempt her from the God whose people she had oppressed.
offenseFull: Babylon said that she would be a lady for ever. Though the Lord had delivered His people into her hand, she showed no mercy and laid a heavy yoke upon the aged. Permission to conquer was not permission for limitless cruelty.

She trusted in wickedness, saying that none saw her, and let wisdom and knowledge turn her aside. Her boast, “I am, and none else beside me,” joined self-exaltation with confidence that she would never know widowhood or the loss of children. Sorceries and astrologers were summoned to secure a future she would not consider humbly.
judgmentFull: The Lord commanded her to sit in the dust and announced the loss of her former honor. Widowhood and loss of children would come suddenly despite her enchantments. An evil she could not ward off would expose the weakness of the wisdom in which she trusted.

The astrologers would be as stubble before fire, unable to deliver even themselves. Those with whom she had labored would wander away, leaving none to save her. The oracle reverses Babylon's confidence at every point: power, learning, commerce, and sorcery could not exempt her from the God whose people she had oppressed.

verses.text: Sit thou silent, and get thee into darkness, O daughter of the Chaldeans: for thou shalt no more be called, The lady of kingdoms.
I was wroth with my people, I have polluted mine inheritance, and given them into thine hand: thou didst shew them no mercy; upon the ancient hast thou very heavily laid thy yoke.
And thou saidst, I shall be a lady for ever: so that thou didst not lay these things to thy heart, neither didst remember the latter end of it.

Therefore hear now this, thou that art given to pleasures, that dwellest carelessly, that sayest in thine heart, I am, and none else beside me; I shall not sit as a widow, neither shall I know the loss of children:

But these two things shall come to thee in a moment in one day, the loss of children, and widowhood: they shall come upon thee in their perfection for the multitude of thy sorceries, and for the great abundance of thine enchantments.
For thou hast trusted in thy wickedness: thou hast said, None seeth me. Thy wisdom and thy knowledge, it hath perverted thee; and thou hast said in thine heart, I am, and none else beside me.

Therefore shall evil come upon thee; thou shalt not know from whence it riseth: and mischief shall fall upon thee; thou shalt not be able to put it off: and desolation shall come upon thee suddenly, which thou shalt not know.
Behold, I will stir up the Medes against them, which shall not regard silver; and as for gold, they shall not delight in it.
Their bows also shall dash the young men to pieces; and they shall have no pity on the fruit of the womb; their eye shall not spare children.
And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beauty of the Chaldees’ excellency, shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.
It shall never be inhabited, neither shall it be dwelt in from generation to generation: neither shall the Arabian pitch tent there; neither shall the shepherds make their fold there.
But wild beasts of the desert shall lie there; and their houses shall be full of doleful creatures; and owls shall dwell there, and satyrs shall dance there.
And the wild beasts of the islands shall cry in their desolate houses, and dragons in their pleasant palaces: and her time is near to come, and her days shall not be prolonged.
That thou shalt take up this proverb against the king of Babylon, and say, How hath the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased!
The Lord hath broken the staff of the wicked, and the sceptre of the rulers.
He who smote the people in wrath with a continual stroke, he that ruled the nations in anger, is persecuted, and none hindereth.
The whole earth is at rest, and is quiet: they break forth into singing.
Yea, the fir trees rejoice at thee, and the cedars of Lebanon, saying, Since thou art laid down, no feller is come up against us.

Hell from beneath is moved for thee to meet thee at thy coming: it stirreth up the dead for thee, even all the chief ones of the earth; it hath raised up from their thrones all the kings of the nations.
All they shall speak and say unto thee, Art thou also become weak as we? art thou become like unto us?
Thy pomp is brought down to the grave, and the noise of thy viols: the worm is spread under thee, and the worms cover thee.
How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!
For thou hast said in thine heart, I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God: I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north:
I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the most High.
Yet thou shalt be brought down to hell, to the sides of the pit.

Call together the archers against Babylon: all ye that bend the bow, camp against it round about; let none thereof escape: recompense her according to her work; according to all that she hath done, do unto her: for she hath been proud against the Lord, against the Holy One of Israel.
Therefore shall her young men fall in the streets, and all her men of war shall be cut off in that day, saith the Lord.
Behold, I am against thee, O thou most proud, saith the Lord God of hosts: for thy day is come, the time that I will visit thee.
And the most proud shall stumble and fall, and none shall raise him up: and I will kindle a fire in his cities, and it shall devour all round about him.
And I will render unto Babylon and to all the inhabitants of Chaldea all their evil that they have done in Zion in your sight, saith the Lord.

Behold, I am against thee, O destroying mountain, saith the Lord, which destroyest all the earth: and I will stretch out mine hand upon thee, and roll thee down from the rocks, and will make thee a burnt mountain.
And they shall not take of thee a stone for a corner, nor a stone for foundations; but thou shalt be desolate for ever, saith the Lord.

Nebuchadrezzar the king of Babylon hath devoured me, he hath crushed me, he hath made me an empty vessel, he hath swallowed me up like a dragon, he hath filled his belly with my delicates, he hath cast me out.
The violence done to me and to my flesh be upon Babylon, shall the inhabitant of Zion say; and my blood upon the inhabitants of Chaldea, shall Jerusalem say.
Therefore thus saith the Lord; Behold, I will plead thy cause, and take vengeance for thee; and I will dry up her sea, and make her springs dry.

Shall not all these take up a parable against him, and a taunting proverb against him, and say, Woe to him that increaseth that which is not his! how long? and to him that ladeth himself with thick clay!
Shall they not rise up suddenly that shall bite thee, and awake that shall vex thee, and thou shalt be for booties unto them?
Because thou hast spoiled many nations, all the remnant of the people shall spoil thee; because of men’s blood, and for the violence of the land, of the city, and of all that dwell therein.
How much she hath glorified herself, and lived deliciously, so much torment and sorrow give her: for she saith in her heart, I sit a queen, and am no widow, and shall see no sorrow.
Therefore shall her plagues come in one day, death, and mourning, and famine; and she shall be utterly burned with fire: for strong is the Lord God who judgeth her.

entries.commentary: The burden of Babylon which Isaiah the son of Amoz did see: lift up a banner upon the high mountain, exalt the voice, shake the hand that they may go into the gates of the nobles. The banner is the Bible. The Most High has commanded His sanctified ones and called His mighty ones for His anger. There is the noise of a multitude in the mountains, kingdoms of nations gathered together; the Most High of hosts musters the host of the battle. They come from a far country, from the end of heaven, the Most High and the weapons of His indignation, to destroy the whole land. Those nukes are not just sitting there for nothing; they will be used.

Howl, for the day of the Most High is at hand; it comes as a destruction from the Almighty. Every hand faints, every heart melts, and pain and sorrow take hold of them. If you study this Bible, you understand the prophecies and what is to come, so you prepare your mind. The ones who should be afraid are those who do not know what is coming to pass. They shall be amazed one at another, their faces as flames. Esau's face is going to be as flames, meaning it is going to be red. The day of the Most High comes cruel with wrath and fierce anger to lay the land desolate and destroy the sinners out of it, those not keeping His laws, which is why the remnant keeping His law escapes and is recovered the second time.

The stars of heaven and the constellations, the satellites, shall not give their light; the sun is darkened and the moon does not shine. The Most High will punish the world for their evil and the wicked for their iniquity, and cause the arrogancy of the proud to cease. The arrogant one is Esau, a very proud nation. The Most High will make a man more precious than fine gold, even a man than the golden wedge of Ophir. This is the Israelite man made precious as fine gold. He shakes the heavens, and the earth removes out of her place off its axis, and what removes it is nuclear destruction, in the day of His fierce anger. Every man turns to his own people and flees into his own land; that is a word against interracial marriage. Everyone found with the other nations, especially Edom, shall be thrust through, everyone joined to them shall fall by the sword, their children dashed to pieces before their eyes, their houses spoiled and their wives ravished. This is not talking about us; it is about these other nations.

The Most High stirs up the Medes against them, who do not regard silver nor delight in gold. Their bows dash the young men to pieces; they have no pity on the fruit of the womb and their eye does not spare children. Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beauty of the Chaldees' excellency, shall be as when the Most High overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah. That is how the United States of Babylon is going to be. It shall never be inhabited from generation to generation; no Arabian pitches a tent there, no shepherd folds there, but wild beasts, owls, satyrs, and dragons dwell in the desolate houses and pleasant palaces. Her time is near to come and her days shall not be prolonged. We do not have that much time, Israel; we have to gather ourselves together, a nation that is not desired. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry)

The Most High will have mercy on Jacob and will yet choose Israel and set them in their own land, and the stranger shall be joined with them and cleave to the house of Jacob. The people that took Israel captive shall be taken by Israel, and the house of Israel shall possess them in the Most High's land for servants and handmaids. Those who once held Israel as captives will become their captives, and Israel shall rule over their oppressors.

In the day the Most High gives Israel rest from sorrow, fear, and the hard bondage in which they were made to serve, they shall take up this proverb against the king of Babylon: How has the oppressor ceased, and the golden city ceased. The Most High has broken the staff of the wicked and the scepter of the rulers, the one who smote the people in wrath with a continual stroke and ruled the nations in anger. Now the whole earth is at rest and quiet and breaks forth into singing. Even the fir trees and the cedars of Lebanon rejoice, saying that since the oppressor is laid down, no feller is come up against them.

Hell from beneath is moved to meet the king of Babylon at his coming; it stirs up the dead for him, even the chief ones of the earth, and raises up from their thrones all the kings of the nations. They speak and say to him, Are you also become weak as we are, are you become like us. His pomp is brought down to the grave and the noise of his viols, the worm is spread under him, and the worms cover him.

How is he fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning, cut down to the ground, he that weakened the nations. He said in his heart that he would ascend into heaven, exalt his throne above the stars of God, sit upon the mount of the congregation in the sides of the north, ascend above the heights of the clouds, and be like the Most High. For all that pride, he shall be brought down to hell, to the sides of the pit.

They that see him shall look narrowly upon him and consider him, saying, Is this the man that made the earth to tremble, that did shake kingdoms. This is the one that made the world as a wilderness, destroyed the cities thereof, and opened not the house of his prisoners.

All the kings of the nations lie in glory, every one in his own house, but this king is cast out of his grave like an abominable branch, as the raiment of those that are slain, thrust through with a sword, going down to the stones of the pit as a carcass trodden under feet. He shall not be joined with them in burial because he destroyed his land and slew his people; the seed of evildoers shall never be renowned.

Prepare slaughter for his children for the iniquity of their fathers, that they do not rise, possess the land, nor fill the face of the world with cities. The Most High of hosts will rise up against Babylon and cut off the name and remnant, and son and nephew. He will make it a possession for the bittern and pools of water and sweep it with the besom of destruction. The besom is a broom made of twigs tied around a stick; sweeping Babylon with the besom of destruction means sweeping it away with the broom of destruction, wiped out completely.

The Most High of hosts has sworn that as He has thought, so shall it come to pass, and as He has purposed, so shall it stand: He will break the Assyrian in His land and upon His mountains tread him underfoot. Then the Assyrian's yoke shall depart from off Israel and his burden from off their shoulders. This is the purpose purposed upon the whole earth, and the hand stretched out upon all the nations; when the Most High has purposed, none shall disallow it, and when His hand is stretched out, none shall turn it back.

In the year king Ahaz died came this burden: Palestine is warned not to rejoice because the rod that smote her is broken, for out of the serpent's root shall come a cockatrice, and its fruit a fiery flying serpent. The firstborn of the poor shall feed and the needy lie down in safety, but the Most High will kill Palestine's root with famine and slay her remnant. The whole of Palestine is called to howl, for a smoke comes from the north and none shall be alone in his appointed times. The answer to the messengers of the nation is that the Most High has founded Zion, and the poor of His people shall trust in it.

This is the word the Lord spoke against Babylon and the land of the Chaldeans. Declare among the nations, publish and set up a standard: Babylon is taken, Bel is confounded, and her idols are broken in pieces. Set up a standard means lift up the greatest standard ever placed on earth, the Bible. The laws show us where we are evil and where we can do better; the Bible is our law and our banner. The scriptures are twofold, so this speaks against ancient Babylon and against modern-day Babylon, which is America. -
Out of the north comes a nation against Babylon to make her land desolate. None shall dwell therein; both man and beast remove and depart.

In those days the children of Israel and the children of Judah come together, going and weeping, to seek the Lord their God. Our people only look for the Most High when we are afflicted, not when things are good. They ask the way to Zion with their faces that direction, saying, come and let us join ourselves to the Lord in a perpetual covenant. There will come a day when we stop seeking the white man through protesting, marching, and voting, and are gathered together only by the word of God. -

My people have been lost sheep whose shepherds caused them to go astray. The so-called reverends and prosperity preachers are bald-headed, beardless, and do nothing the Bible says, turning the people from mountain to hill until they forget their resting place. Their adversaries say, we offend not, because they have sinned against the Lord. Our enemies know that when Israel sins the Most High will not fight for us, and to some degree they are right. The word is to remove out of the midst of Babylon and go forth from the land of the Chaldeans, coming out of her ways and her religions and back to the commandments. -

The Most High raises an assembly of great nations from the north country against Babylon, and none of their arrows return in vain. Chaldea becomes a spoil, and all that spoil her are satisfied. Because Babylon was glad and rejoiced as the destroyers of the Most High's heritage, grown fat as a heifer at grass, her mother shall be confounded. This also touches Esau, the daughter of Babylon, who becomes a wilderness and a dry land, astonishing everyone who passes by.

Put yourselves in array against Babylon, all you that bend the bow; spare no arrows, for she has sinned against the Lord. Take vengeance upon her; as she has done, do unto her. Cut off the sower and the reaper from Babylon, for they shall turn every one to his people and flee every one to his own land. The realest place on earth is jail, where whites stay with whites and Asians with Asians, because everyone turns to their own tribe for protection; the Most High created every species and every nation distinct. -

Israel is a scattered sheep the lions have driven away; first the king of Assyria devoured him, and last Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon broke his bones. The Most High will punish the king of Babylon as he punished Assyria. He will bring Israel again to his habitation to feed on Carmel and Bashan. In those days the iniquity of Israel shall be sought for and there shall be none, and the sins of Judah shall not be found, for he will pardon whom he reserves.

Go up against the land of Merathaim and against Pekod; waste and utterly destroy. How is the hammer of the whole earth cut asunder and broken, and Babylon become a desolation among the nations? The Most High laid a snare and Babylon was taken unaware, because she strove against the Lord. He has opened his armory and brought forth the weapons of his indignation. Every missile, nuke, and bomb these nations think they own, the Most High calls his armory. A black man, the Most High God, and his son Christ are the most powerful beings, and all that the nations possess belongs to him. -

Come against her from the utmost border, open her storehouses, and destroy her utterly; slay all her bullocks and let them go to the slaughter, for their day is come. The voice of them that flee out of Babylon declares in Zion the vengeance of the Lord, the vengeance of his temple. Zion is the temple of the Lord, which is his people.

Call together the archers against Babylon; camp against it round about and let none escape. Recompense her according to her work, for she has been proud against the Holy One of Israel. Her young men shall fall in the streets and all her men of war be cut off in that day. There are many teenagers and young men in Esau's army, and this is why so many of their young men are put to death.

Behold, the Most High is against thee, O thou most proud, for thy day is come. The most proud shall stumble and fall, and none shall raise him up, and a fire is kindled in his cities that devours all around him.

The children of Israel and the children of Judah were oppressed together. That is the so-called blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans, seen together in the ghettos, projects, and slums, last hired and first fired. All that took them captive held them fast and refused to let them go, but their Redeemer is strong; the Lord of hosts is his name, and he will thoroughly plead their cause. The other nations fare well among us because we give them our business, while we own no banks, no Walmarts, and support neither our own businesses nor one another.

A sword is upon the Chaldeans, upon her princes and wise men, upon her liars, her mighty men, her horses and chariots, and upon all the mingled people, the melting pot, and they shall become as women. A sword is upon her treasures and they shall be robbed, and a drought is upon her waters and they shall be dried up, for it is a land of graven images, and they are mad upon their idols.

The wild beasts of the desert and the owl shall dwell there, and it shall be inhabited no more from generation to generation. This is a future prophecy, because ancient Babylon in Iraq still has people living there now. As the Most High overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah and the neighboring cities, so shall no man abide there, neither shall any son of man dwell therein.

A people comes from the north, a great nation and many kings raised up from the coasts of the earth; they are cruel and will not show mercy, set in array like men to the battle against the daughter of Babylon. Who is the daughter of Babylon? It is Edom. The king of Babylon hears the report of them and his hands wax feeble, and anguish takes hold of him as a woman in travail. -

He shall come up like a lion from the swelling of Jordan against the habitation of the strong, but the Most High makes them suddenly run away; who is the chosen man he will appoint over her? Hear the counsel of the Lord against Babylon: surely the least of the flock shall draw them out and make their habitation desolate. At the noise of the taking of Babylon, the earth is moved and the cry is heard among the nations.

The Most High raises against Babylon a destroying wind and sends fanners to fan her and empty her land. Spare not her young men; destroy utterly all her host. The slain fall in the land of the Chaldeans, thrust through in her streets, for Israel has not been forsaken, nor Judah of his God, though their land was filled with sin against the Holy One of Israel.

Israel and Judah have not been forsaken of the Most High. Flee out of the midst of Babylon and deliver every man his soul; do not be cut off in her iniquity, for this is the time of the Lord's vengeance. -

Babylon has been a golden cup in the Lord's hand that made all the earth drunken; the nations drank of her wine and are mad. All the nations partook, and even the children of Israel were made to drink of the cup of our own destruction. Babylon is suddenly fallen and destroyed. We would have healed Babylon, but she is not healed; forsake her, and let everyone go into his own country.
Her judgment reaches unto heaven and is lifted up even to the skies. The Most High has brought forth our righteousness; come, and let us declare in Zion the work of the Lord our God.

Make bright the arrows and gather the shields; the Lord has raised up the spirit of the kings of the Medes, for his device against Babylon is to destroy it, the vengeance of his temple. Set up the standard upon the walls of Babylon, make the watch strong, set the watchmen, and prepare the ambushes. The standard is the Bible, and the men are made ready, for the Most High has both devised and done what he spoke.

Babylon dwells upon many waters, abundant in treasures, but thine end is come. She dwells upon many waters because her embassies reach into every land, from South Africa to Europe to the Philippines; her treasure was built on the backs of the slaves and the stolen Western Hemisphere. The Lord of hosts has sworn to fill her with men as with caterpillars who lift up a shout against her. She is destroyed from within, because being a melting pot, the other nations infiltrate and destroy America from the inside out, the way a caterpillar becomes an infestation that devours a whole land.

He made the earth by his power, established the world by his wisdom, and stretched out the heavens by his understanding; he brings the wind out of his treasures. Every man is brutish in his knowledge, and every founder is confounded by the graven image, for his molten image is falsehood and there is no breath in them. But the portion of Jacob is not like them, for he is the former of all things, and Israel is the rod of his inheritance.

Thou art my battle-ax and weapons of war; with thee the Most High breaks in pieces the nations and destroys kingdoms, the horse and his rider, the chariot and his rider. With thee he breaks in pieces man and woman, old and young, the young man and the maid, the shepherd and his flock, the husbandman and his oxen, and the captains and rulers. The sisters who love feminism had better humble down, because the woman is named right alongside the man. -

The Most High will render unto Babylon and to all the inhabitants of Chaldea all the evil they have done in Zion. Behold, he is against thee, O destroying mountain that destroys all the earth. He will stretch out his hand, roll her down from the rocks, and make her a burnt mountain; they shall take of her no stone for a corner nor foundation, but she shall be desolate forever.

Set up a standard in the land, blow the trumpet among the nations, and prepare the nations against her; call the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz, and appoint a captain against her. Prepare the nations with the king of the Medes, the captains, the rulers, and all the land of his dominion against Babylon.

The land trembles and sorrows, for every purpose of the Lord is performed against Babylon to make it a desolation without inhabitant. The mighty men of Babylon forbear to fight and remain in their holds; their might fails and they become as women. One post runs to meet another to tell the king of Babylon that his city is taken at one end and the passages are stopped. The daughter of Babylon is like a threshing floor; it is time to thresh her, and the time of her harvest shall come.

Nebuchadnezzar has devoured Israel, crushed her, made her an empty vessel, and swallowed her like a dragon. Let the violence done to Zion be upon Babylon, and her blood upon the inhabitants of Chaldea. The Most High will plead Zion's cause, take vengeance for her, and dry up Babylon's sea and springs. Babylon shall become heaps, a dwelling place for dragons, an astonishment and a hissing without inhabitant.

They roar together like lions and yell as lions' whelps. In their heat the Most High makes their feasts and makes them drunken, that they may sleep a perpetual sleep and not wake. He brings them down like lambs to the slaughter, like rams with the he-goats.

How is Sheshach taken, the praise of the whole earth surprised, and Babylon become an astonishment among the nations? The sea is come up upon Babylon, covered with the multitude of its waves. Her cities are a desolation, a dry land and a wilderness, where no man dwells and no son of man passes by.

The Most High will punish Bel in Babylon and bring out of his mouth what he has swallowed, and the wall of Babylon shall fall. My people, go out of the midst of her and deliver every man his soul from the fierce anger of the Lord. A rumor shall come one year and another rumor the next, with violence in the land and ruler against ruler. Do not let your heart faint at the rumor that is heard.

The days come when the Most High does judgment upon the graven images of Babylon, and her whole land is confounded and her slain fall in her midst. Then heaven and earth and all in them sing for Babylon, for the spoiler comes from the north. As Babylon caused the slain of Israel to fall, so at Babylon shall fall the slain of all the earth.

Ye that have escaped the sword, go away, stand not still, remember the Lord afar off, and let Jerusalem come into your mind. We are confounded because strangers have come into the sanctuaries of the Lord's house. Though Babylon should mount up to heaven and fortify the height of her strength, yet from the Most High shall spoilers come unto her.

A cry and great destruction come from Babylon, for the Lord has spoiled her. Her mighty men are taken and their bows broken, and the Lord of recompense shall surely requite. He makes drunk her princes, wise men, captains, rulers, and mighty men, that they sleep a perpetual sleep and not wake. The broad walls of Babylon shall be utterly broken and her high gates burned with fire, and the people shall labor in vain.

Jeremiah commanded Seraiah, when he went with Zedekiah to Babylon, to read all the evil written against Babylon and then declare that the Most High has spoken to cut off this place forever. After reading the book, Seraiah was to bind a stone to it and cast it into the midst of the Euphrates, saying, thus shall Babylon sink and not rise from the evil the Most High brings upon her. Thus far are the words of Jeremiah. Rejoice in the destruction of our enemies, which is the salvation of the righteous. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

I will stand upon my watch, and set me upon the tower, and will watch to see what he will say unto me, and what I shall answer when I am reproved. Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it. For the vision is yet for an appointed time, but at the end it shall speak, and not lie: though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come, it will not tarry. Behold, his soul which is lifted up is not upright in him: but the just shall live by his faith.

Woe to him that increaseth that which is not his! how long? and to him that ladeth himself with thick clay! Because thou hast spoiled many nations, all the remnant of the people shall spoil thee; because of men's blood, and for the violence of the land, of the city, and of all that dwell therein. Woe to him that coveteth an evil covetousness to his house, that he may set his nest on high, that he may be delivered from the power of evil! For the stone shall cry out of the wall, and the beam out of the timber shall answer it.

Woe to him that buildeth a town with blood, and stablisheth a city by iniquity! The people shall labour in the very fire, and the people shall weary themselves for very vanity. For the earth shall be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the Lord, as the waters cover the sea. Woe unto him that giveth his neighbour drink, that puttest thy bottle to him, and makest him drunken also, that thou mayest look on their nakedness! What profiteth the graven image that the maker thereof hath graven it; the molten image, and a teacher of lies, that the maker of his work trusteth therein, to make dumb idols? Woe unto him that saith to the wood, Awake; to the dumb stone, Arise, it shall teach! Behold, it is laid over with gold and silver, and there is no breath at all in the midst of it. But the Lord is in his holy temple: let all the earth keep silence before him. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high)

text.text: Sit thou silent, and get thee into darkness, O daughter of the Chaldeans: for thou shalt no more be called, The lady of kingdoms.
I was wroth with my people, I have polluted mine inheritance, and given them into thine hand: thou didst shew them no mercy; upon the ancient hast thou very heavily laid thy yoke.
And thou saidst, I shall be a lady for ever: so that thou didst not lay these things to thy heart, neither didst remember the latter end of it.

Therefore hear now this, thou that art given to pleasures, that dwellest carelessly, that sayest in thine heart, I am, and none else beside me; I shall not sit as a widow, neither shall I know the loss of children:

But these two things shall come to thee in a moment in one day, the loss of children, and widowhood: they shall come upon thee in their perfection for the multitude of thy sorceries, and for the great abundance of thine enchantments.
For thou hast trusted in thy wickedness: thou hast said, None seeth me. Thy wisdom and thy knowledge, it hath perverted thee; and thou hast said in thine heart, I am, and none else beside me.

Therefore shall evil come upon thee; thou shalt not know from whence it riseth: and mischief shall fall upon thee; thou shalt not be able to put it off: and desolation shall come upon thee suddenly, which thou shalt not know.
Behold, I will stir up the Medes against them, which shall not regard silver; and as for gold, they shall not delight in it.
Their bows also shall dash the young men to pieces; and they shall have no pity on the fruit of the womb; their eye shall not spare children.
And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beauty of the Chaldees’ excellency, shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.
It shall never be inhabited, neither shall it be dwelt in from generation to generation: neither shall the Arabian pitch tent there; neither shall the shepherds make their fold there.
But wild beasts of the desert shall lie there; and their houses shall be full of doleful creatures; and owls shall dwell there, and satyrs shall dance there.
And the wild beasts of the islands shall cry in their desolate houses, and dragons in their pleasant palaces: and her time is near to come, and her days shall not be prolonged.
That thou shalt take up this proverb against the king of Babylon, and say, How hath the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased!
The Lord hath broken the staff of the wicked, and the sceptre of the rulers.
He who smote the people in wrath with a continual stroke, he that ruled the nations in anger, is persecuted, and none hindereth.
The whole earth is at rest, and is quiet: they break forth into singing.
Yea, the fir trees rejoice at thee, and the cedars of Lebanon, saying, Since thou art laid down, no feller is come up against us.

Hell from beneath is moved for thee to meet thee at thy coming: it stirreth up the dead for thee, even all the chief ones of the earth; it hath raised up from their thrones all the kings of the nations.
All they shall speak and say unto thee, Art thou also become weak as we? art thou become like unto us?
Thy pomp is brought down to the grave, and the noise of thy viols: the worm is spread under thee, and the worms cover thee.
How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!
For thou hast said in thine heart, I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God: I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north:
I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the most High.
Yet thou shalt be brought down to hell, to the sides of the pit.

Call together the archers against Babylon: all ye that bend the bow, camp against it round about; let none thereof escape: recompense her according to her work; according to all that she hath done, do unto her: for she hath been proud against the Lord, against the Holy One of Israel.
Therefore shall her young men fall in the streets, and all her men of war shall be cut off in that day, saith the Lord.
Behold, I am against thee, O thou most proud, saith the Lord God of hosts: for thy day is come, the time that I will visit thee.
And the most proud shall stumble and fall, and none shall raise him up: and I will kindle a fire in his cities, and it shall devour all round about him.
And I will render unto Babylon and to all the inhabitants of Chaldea all their evil that they have done in Zion in your sight, saith the Lord.

Behold, I am against thee, O destroying mountain, saith the Lord, which destroyest all the earth: and I will stretch out mine hand upon thee, and roll thee down from the rocks, and will make thee a burnt mountain.
And they shall not take of thee a stone for a corner, nor a stone for foundations; but thou shalt be desolate for ever, saith the Lord.

Nebuchadrezzar the king of Babylon hath devoured me, he hath crushed me, he hath made me an empty vessel, he hath swallowed me up like a dragon, he hath filled his belly with my delicates, he hath cast me out.
The violence done to me and to my flesh be upon Babylon, shall the inhabitant of Zion say; and my blood upon the inhabitants of Chaldea, shall Jerusalem say.
Therefore thus saith the Lord; Behold, I will plead thy cause, and take vengeance for thee; and I will dry up her sea, and make her springs dry.

Shall not all these take up a parable against him, and a taunting proverb against him, and say, Woe to him that increaseth that which is not his! how long? and to him that ladeth himself with thick clay!
Shall they not rise up suddenly that shall bite thee, and awake that shall vex thee, and thou shalt be for booties unto them?
Because thou hast spoiled many nations, all the remnant of the people shall spoil thee; because of men’s blood, and for the violence of the land, of the city, and of all that dwell therein.
How much she hath glorified herself, and lived deliciously, so much torment and sorrow give her: for she saith in her heart, I sit a queen, and am no widow, and shall see no sorrow.
Therefore shall her plagues come in one day, death, and mourning, and famine; and she shall be utterly burned with fire: for strong is the Lord God who judgeth her.
